sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the map panel
sections.what: Brings in the React hooks, the village simulation engine, the language helper and the translated text table.
sections.why: Likely reason: the map panel needs its drawing engine and its language text.

sections.name: CaseMapTile (part 1)
sections.title: Map setup, zoom and layer controls
sections.what: Reads the language text, keeps references to the map host and its canvases, and starts the village engine when the panel appears and stops it when the panel leaves. Holds the zoom level and the on or off setting for each layer. Zoom stays between 1 and 1.8, and fit resets to 1.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared engine draws the village, and this panel only hands it the screen elements to draw on.
sections.watch_out: The mini canvas may be missing, and the engine is still given whatever reference is there.

sections.name: CaseMapTile (part 2)
sections.title: Map picture and boundary layers
sections.what: Draws a painted village scene with three outlines of the same parcel: a shaded red historical boundary, a green survey boundary, and a dotted map boundary. The parcel label DEMO-456 sits in the middle. Each outline can be hidden or shown, so a viewer can compare the boundaries.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tile shows the same land three ways so a viewer can see where the records disagree. Reason for the fixed drawing coordinates not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The shapes, label and aria text are fixed in the code, so they will not change when the real parcel data changes.

sections.name: CaseMapTile (part 3)
sections.title: Layer toggle buttons and fit button
sections.what: Shows three toggle buttons, one for each boundary, with a colour dot and a label. A small button in the corner resets the view to fit the parcel. Each toggle button reports whether it is on.
sections.why: Lets the user switch boundaries on and off without leaving the page. The fit button brings the view back if the user zooms or moves it.
sections.watch_out: The toggle state must match the layer visibility in the drawing above, or a button can show on while its boundary stays hidden.

sections.name: CaseMapTile (part 4)
sections.title: Floating area summary card
sections.what: When shown, displays a small card with a sparkline, a fixed area of 0.18 acres, and two buttons. One button jumps to the differences section, or calls a supplied handler. The other button closes the card.
sections.why: Gives a quick summary of the area gap and a shortcut to the explanation of differences.
sections.watch_out: The 0.18 acres figure and the bar heights are typed in, not calculated, so they can disagree with the real area.

sections.name: CaseMapTile (part 5)
sections.title: Small corner preview canvas
sections.what: Places a 148 by 148 pixel canvas in the corner for a small preview of the parcel. It is hidden from screen readers because it is decorative.
sections.why: Likely reason: a compact overview of the parcel. Drawing is done elsewhere, through the mini canvas reference.
sections.watch_out: Nothing in this section draws onto the canvas, so it stays blank if the drawing code is missing or fails.

summary: A map panel that starts a shared village drawing engine and offers zoom, fit and layer controls. Only its opening part is visible in this packet.
purpose: Shows a village map with controls for zoom, fitting the view and turning map layers on or off.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the full design. The visible parts suggest a demo map with historical, survey and map-detail layers.
how: Reads the language text, keeps references to the map host and its canvases, starts the village engine when the panel appears and stops it when the panel leaves. Zoom keeps the scale between 1 and 1.8, fit resets it to 1, and the layer toggles flip the historical, survey and map-detail layers. The rest of the rendering is not visible in the packet.
inputs: An optional callback named onGoDiff, passed from the parent screen.
outputs: A map panel on screen. The rendering details are not visible in the packet.
risks: The map depends on a canvas and the shared engine, so if registration fails nothing is drawn. The visible part does not show the rendering, so the full display cannot be checked from these notes.
debug: If the map is blank, check the engine registration in the village canvas code and that the host and canvas references are set.
